description: IT band soreness coming on after a long run — Dean must not prescribe intensity, should flag the spike risk, give IT band-specific prehab, and NOT set plan_action.injury_hold.

user.name: Priya
user.injury_notes: IT band tightness — outer knee soreness reported after long runs

inbound_sms: That 11 miler felt pretty solid but my outer knee is a bit sore now — started around mile 8. Feels like it might be IT band? Happened to me once before a couple years ago.

ground_truth.notes: IT band soreness coming on after the long run jumped from 9→11 miles (22% increase in a single session). All 4 training days for the week are already done (runs_this_week=4, today is Sunday) — Dean MUST explicitly acknowledge the week is complete and that there are no more runs until Monday. Dean should: (1) confirm the IT band read — outer knee tightness starting late in a long run is the classic overuse pattern; (2) give 2-3 IT band-specific prehab actions named explicitly from: hip abductor clamshells 3×15, lateral band walks, foam rolling TFL/outer glute (NOT the IT band directly), hip flexor stretch in lunge position — at least 2 of these named specifically; (3) recommend ice/rest before the next run — 'ice tonight' (not 'ice after your next run' since the week is done), and the next run depends on how it feels; (4) NOT prescribe any additional activity this week (week is complete). plan_action.injury_hold would be an overreaction — the athlete can still run easy next week if it settles. plan_action.lighter_week is acceptable. Response should NOT contain generic advice. Core pass criteria (score 7+): week-complete acknowledgment + at least 2 named IT band exercises + 'ice tonight' or equivalent immediate care recommendation.
